title: Conditional followed by a continuation
statement: Fix a program environment, resource limits, and execution depth. Let $c$ be a condition and let $s_1,s_2,s$ be statements. In an initial state $\sigma$, suppose that when $c$ holds, the sequence of $s_1$ followed by $s$ can execute with cost at most $T-(\mathrm{cost}(c)+1)$ to a state satisfying $Q$, and that when $c$ does not hold, the corresponding sequence using $s_2$ can do so. If $c$ is safe in $\sigma$ and $\mathrm{cost}(c)+1\le T$, then the conditional with branches $s_1,s_2$, followed by $s$, can execute from $\sigma$ with cost at most $T$ to a state satisfying $Q$.
hypotheses_covered: If $c$ holds in $\sigma$, the sequence of $s_1$ followed by $s$ has an execution of cost at most $T-(\mathrm{cost}(c)+1)$ ending in a state satisfying $Q$
If $c$ does not hold in $\sigma$, the sequence of $s_2$ followed by $s$ has an execution of cost at most $T-(\mathrm{cost}(c)+1)$ ending in a state satisfying $Q$
